extracted_context.summary_text: Multi Asset Research Asia Equity Research MIM EMEA Korea Conviction Update September 2025 Korea is moderately unattractive from an asset class level perspective, while it is fairly valued from an MER perspective, leading to an overall score of Medium. Korea is heavily weighted in the Technology Sector, and has extremely large stock concentration, greater even than the US and UK, with the top 10 stocks making up almost 60% of the index, and Samsung alone represent close to 30%. When considering macro or country economic news (such as corporate governance) it is worth noting the stock specific nature of the index may drive returns more than these aggregate events. Korean returns and fundamentals are also becoming more idiosyncratic relative to global fundamentals. Related to the above, we find that the returns are not well explained by their sector exposure. We also find Korean returns and fundamentals are becoming more idiosyncratic relative to global markets. Large stock specific risk that Samsung loses market share given the rapid increase in Chinese memory expertise. Corporate governance reforms in July 2025 to increase shareholder rights increased market optimism. However, it is still too early too see if this will lead to any real positive improvement, and we further estimate that the upside from corporate governance to be in the region of c.1% expected returns. In terms of potential portfolio considerations, we find cash flows are more sensitive relative to global equities than most DM’s, increasing cyclicality risk. Currently, Nominal USD VIRs relative to history are at the 65 th percentile, and Real Local VIRs are at the 59 th percentile. We should be prepared to hold Brazil through the cycle, due to the high persistence of returns.

extracted_context.summary_text: US SMID Conviction Update April 2025 CMA Team Executive Summary Executive Table Executive Summary US Small Caps have different key sector drivers than large caps, with Financial Services, Industrials and Consumer Cyclicals accounting for the majority. They also have lower international revenue exposure and less concentration. We find sector exposure can explain a large proportion of the returns of US Small Caps. However, there has been a divergence YTD, suggesting a more idiosyncratic driver over this shorter period, which we find is coming from sentiment rather than fundamentals. In terms of fundamentals, we find the absolute levels of profitability are lower. Growth, on the other hand is higher and this is what drives the higher PE. We find US Small Caps are more sensitive to macroeconomic variables compared to Large Caps. While we find no evidence of an unconditional small cap premium, we see strong evidence that buying at attractive valuation levels will lead to high forward returns. Conviction Update | U.S. Treasury The Interest–Deficit Loop The worry runs like this: higher yields make the interest bill bigger, a bigger bill widens the deficit, a wider deficit means more borrowing, and more borrowing pushes yields higher again. Yields rise Interest bill rises More borrowing Deficit widens The Holy Trinity of Debt Stability: Growth, Interest and the Primary Balance To test whether the current level of yields are being a threat to debt sustainbaility , we start with the arithmetic that governs the debt ratio. Debt rises when the rate the government pays beats how fast the economy grows, and when it is still borrowing before interest. Both conditions must hold. Growth currently beats the rate we pay, so the debt is not compounding against us on its own. The primary deficit is negative and expected to stay negative, and that is the main driver of a higher debt ratio. extracted_context.summary_text: December 2017 EM Financials Why are we looking at this sector? 2 EM FN is the second largest sector by market capitalisation accounting for approximately 24% of the MSCI EM index. EM FN’s VIR are high, making it a relatively attractive investment opportunity. This supports the overall EM VIR. Since the GFC, EM FN’s assets have grown rapidly and concerns over these assets’ quality have been raised. This has been led by the Chinese government’s large stimulus package to boost external demand. The implications of our current assumptions, was that EM FN’s P/B deserved to trade at a sizeable premium to DM FN book values. We needed to get some comfort around this. Key points 3 Chinese banks have not been immune to poor lending. Government helped tidy up the mess in the late 1990s/ 2000s. The Chinese government is well aware that it needs to reduce the risks building up in the domestic financial system. Following the GFC, government initiated a stimulus package, with formal bank credit used as the distribution mechanism. Alongside the formal bank loans, money from the informal sector was funnelled through financial institutions. This statement by the PBOC governor certainly emphasises the risk in the system: “ China’s financial sector is and will be in a period with high risks that are easily triggered. Under pressure from multiple factors at home and abroad, the risks are multiple, broad, hidden, complex, sudden, contagious, and hazardous. The structural unbalance is salient; law-breaking and disorders are rampant; latent risks are accumulating; [and the financial system’s] vulnerability is obviously increasing. [China] should prevent both the “black swan” events and the “gray rhino” risks.” Government will look to tighten liquidity, encouraging more market determined credit allocation and remove the protection that inefficient SOEs enjoy. Despite strict lending standards, Chinese banks used loopholes to grow off-balance sheet debt. WMPs is one such shadow banking product that has ballooned, investing in a variety of assets. extracted_context.summary_text: Equity Market Review: Japan We are neutral on Japan Equities. DECEMBER 2025 Mark Murray, CFA Head of Capital Market Assumptions Morningstar Investment Management Europe LLC Grant Slade, CFA Economist Morningstar Investment Management LLC Lorraine Tan, CFA Director of Equity Research Morningstar Research Services LLC EQUITY MARKET REVIEW | JAPAN Matt Wilson; Ziying Peng, CFA; Nick Parekh; Phoebe Chapman Investment Analyst; Associate Investment Analysts Morningstar Investment Management LLC 48 52 Market Sentiment Appendix Executive Summary Market Overview: Composition Market Overview: Past Performance Economic Outlook: Metrics, Drivers, and Risks Valuation: Asset Class - Level Perspective Valuation: Stock - Level Perspective 3 8 16 21 32 40 EQUITY MARKET REVIEW | JAPAN Executive Summary We assess Japan Equities, combining top-down and bottom-up valuation viewpoints, as well as market sentiment. Japan Equities Look Neutral Overall;Top-Down , Moderately Unattractive View Is Offset by Bottom-Up, Neutral View EXECUTIVE SUMMARY Overall, we are neutral on Japan equities. From a top-down perspective, valuations and profitability are above our long-term assumptions, creating a negative reversion that will impinge future expected returns. On the other hand, Japan equities are fairly valued from a bottom-up perspective based on our analysts’ cash flow outlook. In general, Japan equities present a balanced risk/reward profile. Japan equities are moderately unattractive, with the current P/E ratio slightly above our long-term assumption at 16 times. Current higher profitability is expected to normalize and contribute to a negative valuation reversion over the next decade. ( see Slide 32 for details). Brazil’s economy slowed as inflation rose and investment declined . Emerging Market assets L arge/mega caps appear generally cheaper (India is an exception). But this could be a valuation trap, as many of these larger cap companies comprise government owned or controlled entities, which have traditionally delivered sub-par returns on equity due to competing social interests (such as pursuing economic growth and job stability) North Asia seems less in market favour than South Asia. Companies in South Asia are generally more domestic oriented and more stable earnings growers, while North Asia companies have typically exhibited more cyclical earnings and been more reliant on export markets. Brazil, India, Taiwan, and China appear the most attractively priced. From a sector perspective, managers favour domestic-oriented sectors such as Consumer Staples, and areas that are perceived to be secular growth stories, rather than cyclically exposed sectors such as commodities and “old school” IT. Summary Fundamentals for AREITs remain satisfactory, but not strong. L everage is a little higher (once accounting for asset value rises) than a few years ago. Earnings growth continues to be modest, with a subdued rental outlook in major markets. Valuations for AREITs look less attractive on various valuation metrics following strong price performance Sentiment is very positive towards the sector driven primarily for the search for yield, with property rental fundamentals not looking particularly favourable Proposal to decrease target exposure from 11.6% to 6.6%, using client cash outflows to gradually reduce position. Fundamentals: Earnings growth has been assisted by lower debt funding costs, residential development profits, and increased funds management earnings. As has been the case for several years, property rental growth over the last year was fairly muted, and it is not expected that this will change in the next few years. Recent strength in property valuations appear to be driven more by cap rate compression than rental growth. Property valuations look less attractive from a dividend yield perspective and a range of valuation metrics (P/E, P/NTA and cap rates). Strong interest from offshore buyers for Australian commercial property assets has been driven by low offshore funding costs, relatively high cash yields compared to international assets, and the fall in the AUD. 2. Without making an assumption on how the split between large pharma abd HC Eqpt & Sevices is likely to evolve in the future we take a conservative assumption in setting our fair margins at 14%. We appear to have been more cautious on Europe HC Margins than US HC margins, as demonstrated through larger impairment from historical average. All other player’s margins trends were stable. Overall EBITDA, CFO or Profit Margins have been and are expected to remain on a positive trend. Price declines offset by higher volumes and lower costs 5 Large pharma is shifting out of retail drugs into specialty pharma which is less prone to pricing pressure. Australian Financials 2 Conviction Score Feb 2019 Conviction Level Comment Overall Conviction Low-to-Medium While valuation metrics and contrarian indicators look reasonably attractive , this overall conviction score assigns significant weight to the fundamental risks reviewed in later slides. These risks represent not only a direct threat to Financials sector earnings, but also a “de-rating” risk to the stock prices, because Australian investors haven’t seen extreme underperformance by their own Financials sector since the 1990s recession. Since the near future represents “uncharted territory” for the sector in both business environment and market sentiment, considerable caution is justified. Absolute Valuation Low-to-Medium Despite weak returns in the 4 th quarter of 2018, the latest VIR of Australian Financials at 4.6% is still less than the unconditional return of 6.5%. This conviction rating is justified because the sector is still trading above Fair Value. Relative Valuation Medium Within the opportunity set of global equity markets, a VIR of 4.6% is attractive but not “best in show”. Several developed market sectors appear more compelling: European Financials 5.6%, European Energy 5.3%, European Telcos 4.9% and Australian Telcos 6.5%. US Consumer Staples and Australian Consumer Discretionary have VIRs of ~4.4% and ~4.6% respectively, so are also worthy of consideration. Contrarian Indicators Medium Investor positioning improved after the Financial Services Royal Commission published a surprisingly benign set of final recommendations. Short interest against the banks has reduced since that release, but remains moderate, and a relief rally in the stocks has partially offset some of 2018's poor performance. Earnings expectations are remarkably sanguine, with sell-side analysts generally forecasting a rebound in sector earnings, implying that many of 2018’s challenges were one-offs. According to Morgan Stanley’s broker research team, net flows to US real estate funds have been consistently in net outflow since late 2021. Europe has taken on significant debt and will likely incur value destructive equity raises but the US and UK are likely to avoid any material dilutive raises. Investors have rotated away from Reits due to rising interest rates and due to the risks of economic growth slow down. Ultimately, we are guided by our valuations which show a medium. Central Bank Credibility Remains a Concern
extracted_context.summary_text: Turkey Inflation Refresh March 2019 Impact of Using Consensus Inflation on Turkey Inflation Assumptions The impact of using 2 years of consensus inflation is meaningful for Turkey’s long term average inflation In effect, the 10 year average of 10% is now obtained using a long term estimate of around 8.5%-9.0% The somewhat changes the scope of the estimate and allows us to focus more on what type of number we truly think can be achieved over the long run Turkey CPI Weights 3 Source: Turkish Statistical Institute Historical Success Analysis of Different Regimes Average CPI Median CPI Average Deviation from Target Median Deviation from Target Implicit Inflation Targeting 2002-2005 23.4 17.3 4.6 2.2 Inflation Targeting 2006-2018 9.1 8.7 3.9 3.7 Post GFC Policy-Integrating Financial Stability 2011-2018 9.3 8.5 4.3 3.5 Erdogan Era 7/2014-2018 10.5 9.2 5.5 4.2 Inflation Targeting ex 2017/18 2006-2016 8.3 8.2 3.0 3.1 Post GFC Policy ex 2017/18 2011-2017 7.9 7.8 2.8 2.8 Erdogan Era ex 2017/2018 7/2014-2016 8.0 7.9 3.0 2.9 Central Bank Credibility Remains a Concern It is important to note that while central bank credibility has been an issue for a while in Turkey, the expanded powers given to the executive in 2018 further damaged the ability of the CB to be an independent arm In 2018, President Erdogan claimed the exclusive power to appoint central bank rate-setters and named his son-in-law as overseer of economic policy. This follows several years of departures from his investor friendly team. As part of his election in 2018 that expanded his powers, he promised to take more control over monetary policy. He has repeatedly stated that he believes that keeping borrowing costs low is a priority and that higher rates actually lead to higher inflation. While the central bank did raise rates aggressively in September, 2018 (from 17.75 to 24), Erdogan was critical of the move and let the world know that his patience with these types of moves was limited. Many believe that the current move towards relative orthodoxy is a temporary one.

But this could be a valuation trap, as many of these larger cap companies comprise government owned or controlled entities, which have traditionally delivered sub-par returns on equity due to competing social interests (such as pursuing economic growth and job stability) North Asia seems less in market favour than South Asia. Brazil, India, Taiwan, and China appear the most attractively priced. Implication for companies and investors is that they are banned from engaging in any business activity with the people or firms on the SDN list. Risks: This round of sanctions is expected to have very limited impact. Risk that more people and companies get added to the SDN list has gone up. Can mean more writedowns for Sberbank for instance. Sberbank accounts for 25% of the Russian equity market. Russia is a big commodity producer/exporter so this would be inflationary. ‘Mitigating’ factors: To hurt the Russian economy, US need to touch oil and gas. Problem is this would hurt Europe so unlikely to happen. The more people and companies get added, the more it becomes difficult for companies globally to implement - and to unwind. 5 Investment opportunity – Conviction level Recommendations – Russia April 2018 Conviction Level Comment Overall Conviction Medium to High Russia represents a ‘Medium to High’ conviction opportunity.
